summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, hypoglycemia, and shoulder injury after a fall. The abdominal pain was consistent with acute on chronic pancreatitis, though imaging showed no obstruction or acute surgical findings. He was treated with IV fluids, pain control, and gradual advancement of diet. His blood sugar improved with supportive care, and he was instructed to hold metformin until follow-up and to only take Lantus insulin with full meals. He tolerated oral intake, had stable vital signs, and was discharged home the next day with follow-up instructions and medication adjustments.
